chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The man is flogged the Hadd (prescribed penalty) while standing, and the woman while seated; and every body part is struck, but the head and the genitals are spared.

key_terms.الحد: Hadd — the prescribed legal penalty fixed by divine law, as opposed to discretionary punishment (ta'zir)
key_terms.المذاكير: The sexual/genital organs; plural of 'dhakara'. Exempted from flogging to prevent permanent harm
key_terms.قائماً: Standing; describes the posture of the male recipient of flogging
key_terms.قاعدة: Seated; describes the posture of the female recipient of flogging

ai.seo_question: How is the Hadd flogging penalty administered according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) specifies the procedural details for administering the Hadd flogging penalty for adultery (zina). Men receive the punishment standing while women are seated — a distinction rooted in modesty and bodily protection. The ruling exempts the head and genitals, preventing lethal or permanently disfiguring injury, reflecting the principle that Hadd punishments, while severe, are not meant to kill or permanently maim.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Zurara, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The man would be whipped by the Penalty (Hadd) while standing, and the woman whilst seated, and every body part can be whipped except for the head and the sexual parts’.
